summary: Citizens of the countries and territories exempted on the Foreign Ministry's visa list — including the EU, US, UK, Canada and Australia — can visit Israel for up to 90 days but must obtain an ETA-IL electronic travel authorization before starting their journey; other nationalities need a B/2 visitor visa from an Israeli consulate.

tips.text: The UK FCDO says visitors arriving at Ben Gurion Airport get an entry card instead of a passport stamp; at other entry points you may get a card or a stamp. Keep the card with your passport until you leave — it is evidence that you entered legally, and you may need it if you cross into Palestine.

The UK FCDO lists three land crossings with Jordan — Allenby/King Hussein Bridge, the northern Jordan River/Sheikh Hussein crossing and the southern Yitzhak Rabin/Wadi Araba crossing — and says they may be restricted or closed at short notice. Check the Israel Airports Authority's updates before you go.
The UK FCDO says you may face lengthy personal questioning and baggage searches at security when you enter and leave Israel.
The UK FCDO says Shabbat runs from sunset on Friday to nightfall on Saturday, and advises against driving into ultra-Orthodox areas of Jerusalem on Shabbat, where residents may throw stones at cars.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Israel?
faq.answer: If you are from one of the countries and territories exempted on the Foreign Ministry's visa list — the EU, US, UK, Canada and Australia among them — you do not need a visa for stays of up to 90 days, but you must obtain an ETA-IL electronic travel authorization online before you start your journey. Moldovan citizens are visa-exempt only with a biometric passport, according to the Foreign Ministry. Other nationalities need a B/2 visitor visa from an Israeli embassy or consulate; the Foreign Ministry lists, among others, Afghan, Lebanese, Libyan, Pakistani, Saudi, Somali, Sudanese, Syrian and Yemeni passports as needing a tourist visa.

faq.question: What is ETA-IL and how do I get one?
faq.answer: ETA-IL is Israel's electronic travel authorization; since January 2025 the Population and Immigration Authority requires visitors from visa-exempt countries to obtain one. Apply at israel-entry.piba.gov.il with your passport details; the application fee is 25 NIS. It stays valid for up to two years (or until your passport expires) and allows stays of up to 90 days per visit.

faq.question: Does Israel stamp your passport?
faq.answer: Not at Ben Gurion Airport: the UK FCDO says visitors arriving there get an entry card instead of a passport stamp, while at other entry points you may get either a card or a stamp. The FCDO's advice for Iran says stamps from other countries' border crossings with Israel can also lead to refusal of entry there.

faq.question: Will visiting Israel prevent me from entering other countries?
faq.answer: The UK FCDO says an Israeli stamp or other evidence of travel to Israel may get you refused entry to Iran, Lebanon, Syria and Kuwait — for Iran this includes stamps from other countries' border crossings with Israel — and that a passport showing previous travel to Israel will not be accepted for travel to Libya. It also says visitors entering through Ben Gurion Airport get an entry card instead of a passport stamp.

faq.question: Is it safe to visit Israel right now?
faq.answer: The UK FCDO advises against all travel to Gaza and within 500 m of the border with Gaza, and to parts of northern Israel and the occupied Golan Heights, and says rocket fire can affect most areas of Israel; it tells travellers to check Home Front Command for the latest guidance. Australia's Smartraveller advises reconsidering the need to travel to Israel and not travelling to the border areas with Gaza, Lebanon and Syria.
